o1.biggest_strength: Ties every email to the two retention habits, adds a fifth email that nudges whichever habit is still missing, and uses triggers/skips the tool can actually run.
o1.biggest_mistake: Per-email success bars are soft — it gives the baseline metric but leaves the numeric target to a single global measurement section, so it's unclear what each email must hit to count.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Put a concrete numeric 'worked if' on each email (e.g. recurring-task rate from 14% to 20% in 7 days) rather than only at series level.

o2.biggest_strength: Each email ships with trigger, subject, preview, body, button, goal and a numeric 'worked if', and the drop rationale names the 'perfect on Sunday, gone by Wednesday' trap precisely.
o2.biggest_mistake: The fifth slot is a Pro upsell instead of a nudge toward the still-missing habit, so the sequence stops pushing users toward the 67% both-habits group after email 3.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Spend the fifth email converting one-habit users into both-habit users and move Pro to a later lifecycle point.

reason: Both are accurate, on-brand and use the real triggers, but Output 1 builds the whole arc around reaching both habits — including a fifth email that pushes whichever habit is still missing — while Output 2's fifth email sells Pro instead.
